routeModel.implication: Refresh, back/forward, and deep-link recovery do not preserve stage, tool, results view, map layer, Scenario, Version, or Run context.

Setup.purpose: Common planning configuration plus Scenario workspace

Inventory.purpose: Cell list, map placement, import, and per-cell RF profile

Propagation.purpose: Canonical propagation geometry, optimization entry, and reference panels

Experiments.purpose: Queued parameter sweeps and Pareto comparison

Signal surface.purpose: Current RF surface generation and GIS export

Results.purpose: Current operation result views and map inspection

Data.purpose: Dataset confidence, model assumptions, validation, calibration

Scenario.assessment: Correctly above RF operation, but identity is not persistent in header.

Version.primaryLocation: Setup Scenario workspace and Project menu
Version.assessment: Correctly owns saved inputs, but duplicate save entry points and hidden active identity increase risk.

Inventory.assessment: Related concepts are together; bulk/provenance detail is underdeveloped.

Planning Area.assessment: Spatially appropriate; scope selection can be visually dense.

RF Configuration.assessment: Common inputs are split from per-cell overrides; research inputs are mixed into Propagation.

Simulation.assessment: Run is visible; source Version/Run identity needs persistent treatment.

Optimization.assessment: Capabilities are connected but terminology and target lineage are spread.

Run.assessment: Durable record is under Review as expected; current Run identity is not always visible.

Report.assessment: Correctly a Review output; ordinary UX exposes storage terminology.

Dataset.assessment: Important and visible, but Data combines confidence, packs, model, validation, and calibration.

Diagnostics.assessment: Technically coherent but mixes operational analysis and research/validation.

locations: Scenario revision detail after applying a solution
duplicateEntryPoints.risk: Users may not know whether these save a Project, Scenario, or Version, even though the domain semantics differ.
Related lineage jumps use different copy and are not always accompanied by the same context summary.
Multiple valid entry points can make the source binding ambiguous.
Current result, map evidence, and durable historical evidence are not one visibly named object.

hierarchyConflicts.conflict: RF configuration and Scenario persistence share one drawer.
Canonical RF controls and research/reference studies share one normal scroll path.
Dataset confidence, model assumptions, field validation, and calibration share one Review tool.
Project identity is global while Scenario/Version identity is local to drawers.

currentMermaid:
flowchart LR
  Launch[Open A.T.O.M / map] --> Dataset[Dataset loaded]
  Dataset --> Plan[Plan: Setup + Inventory]
  Plan --> RF[Simulate: Propagation / Signal surface]
  RF --> Inspect[Results: map layers / inspector]
  Inspect --> Optimize[Analyze / optimize: priorities + policy]
  Optimize --> Pareto[Review: Pareto / compare]
  Pareto --> Apply[Apply to new Version or branch]
  Apply --> Save[Project / Scenario / Version save]
  Save --> Report[Review: Report / Run History]
  Report --> Revisit[Open source Version / Run again]

proposedDirection.principle: Keep the current four-stage map shell; add a persistent identity/state context that travels with current results, historical Runs, and Reports.
